reads.page: f633, with archive.org p.638 as second witness
reads.source: Gallica f633, native IIIF, six column-height crops, plus a 3.6x upscaled crop of col 1265A 'stare non potet'; archive.org p.638 rendered at 200 dpi over the left column.
reads.found: THE TWO PRINTINGS DIFFER AT COL 1265A AND NO MARKER IS FIRED. Gallica sets *stare non potet* with the word unmistakably ending -et, and our TEI has *potet*; the archive copy sets *potest* clean. A single word defective on only one printing does not license a public accusation against Migne's type (the 8961 @0317D precedent, and 8950's *Mititte*/*Mittite*), so the English reads 'cannot stand', nothing is marked and nothing is patched. Otherwise no plate/TEI divergence. Vulgate divergences: Is 22:18 *Coronans coronabit te* -- OUR OWN Clementine flat file is corrupt at that verse (*Coronas cornonabit*), so no claim is made either way (crux); Is 22:24 lemma *Et suspendam super* for *Et suspendent super eum* (fired [var:]); Lc 19:48 quoted *Omnis populus pendebat ex eo* (fired [var:]); Is 23:7 *Nunquid non haec vestra est* for *Numquid non vestra haec est* (crux, word order); Ps 136:1 *dum recordaremur* for *cum recordaremur* (crux). Foot of both columns blank.
